source.title: Batch Normalization Is Blind to the First and Second Derivatives of the Loss
source.authors: Zhanpeng Zhou; Wen Shen; Huixin Chen; Ling Tang; YueFeng Chen; Quan-Shi Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests batch normalization's effect on loss derivatives and learned representations, but does not measure training classification error, training speed, or tolerance to learning rates as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports derivative comparisons and representation results, but none measures the convergence or training-speed outcomes named by the claim versions. Cited results from other work are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures BN's filtering of Taylor-expansion loss components and its effects on representations. It reports no training-error, convergence-speed, learning-rate-tolerance, or trainable-depth outcomes testing V1–V6. Its theoretical arguments concern loss information propagation and do not establish that BN fails to accelerate training.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. More precisely, the authors attribute the filtering of shared Taylor-expansion loss components to BN standardization; with differing sample losses, their conclusions concern average gradient and Hessian components. They report impaired discriminative representations in specific settings, propose LN as an alternative there, and explicitly avoid concluding that standardization is generally harmful.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes batch-normalization derivative propagation and learned representations, rather than testing the claim's training-error or speed recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported representation effect differs between batches whose samples share the same analytic loss formula and batches with different labels.

fits_no_version.finding: RealNVP-LN usually assigned higher likelihood to real than interpolated MNIST images, whereas RealNVP-BN did not significantly distinguish them. Appendix I.3 reports similar findings for shallow and narrow variants.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization choice affects real-versus-interpolated-image likelihood discrimination in the tested RealNVP models.

fits_no_version.finding: BN classifiers learned less clustered features with single-category batches; mixed-label BN-base classifiers could learn well-clustered features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN's effect on feature clustering depends on batch label composition in the tested CIFAR-10 classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorems and Tables 1–4 show suppression of shared first-order and diagonal second-order Taylor loss components, with suppression of a component associated with off-diagonal terms.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BN standardization filters particular components of loss information during back-propagation under the paper's decomposition and assumptions.

record.problems: The representation comparisons are qualitative t-SNE visualizations; the paper does not give numeric clustering scores in the supplied text. RealNVP comparisons are also presented as figure-based curves without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No results were omitted under the 60-row limit. Derivative-propagation experiments and cited prior-work results were not extracted because they do not measure outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Zero or near-zero training classification error, including corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, stopping and regularization.
Spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student models and their reduction with extra student neurons.
Training-error degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization exceptions.
Initialization-dependent learning speed, signal propagation and trainable depth.
Loss recovery or divergence across stability thresholds and sharpness trajectories during training.
BN's effects on accuracy gain speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup's normalization-free training speed and stability.

record.verdict_notes: No version-relevant results are missing. Derivative-propagation measurements and representation differences cannot by themselves support or challenge the training outcomes specified by the versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, stopping, and regularization.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization and effects of student width.
Initialization, training speed, and trainable depth.
Training outcomes across learning rates and sharpness.
Accuracy gain speed, learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup training stability.

rows.subject: RealNVP-BN and RealNVP-LN
rows.operation_detail: Compared average log-likelihoods on real and linearly interpolated MNIST images.

conditions.value: specific pairs of categories; pair count not stated

rows.measure: Average log-likelihood across interpolation rate; numeric values are figure only.
rows.uncertainty: Shaded area represents standard deviation; numeric values not stated.
rows.note: The text says LN usually assigned higher log-likelihood to real images than interpolated images, while BN could not significantly distinguish them. The figure reports separate category pairs, but numerical values are not stated.
rows.check: Likelihood discrimination between real and interpolated images does not measure any claim version; partial is therefore inappropriate. Figure 1 shows ten category pairs, rather than an unspecified pair count. The reported comparison is qualitative, without extracted numerical likelihoods.

rows.subject: VGG-11, VGG-16, ResNet-18, ResNet-34, DenseNet-121, and DenseNet-169 variants
rows.operation_detail: Compared t-SNE visualizations of top-FC-layer input features across normalization and batch-label settings.

conditions.value: same analytic loss formula versus different labels
t-SNE visualization; no numeric score stated

rows.baseline: DNN-ori or DNN-LN where available; different-label batch baseline for BN networks
rows.value: With same-formula losses, BN features were described as far less clustered than ori and LN features; with different-label batches, BN-base features could be well clustered.
rows.note: Results are qualitative and reported by model groups; text does not provide separate numeric outcomes for each architecture.
rows.check: Feature clustering does not establish training accuracy or speed. Keep architecture-specific comparators distinct: VGG has ori, BN, LN and ori-base variants; ResNet and DenseNet have BN, LN, BN-base and LN-base variants, without ori variants. The well-clustered BN-base finding concerns the latter architectures.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
